Industry-Specific PPE Solutions for Glass Manufacturing
Hand Line delivers comprehensive personal protective equipment (PPE) solutions tailored to each stage of the glass manufacturing process:
Raw Material Handling & Batching – Controls silica dust, chemical irritation, and ergonomic strain with P3 respirators, chemical- and ergonomic gloves, and dust swabs.
Hot End & Forming – Manages extreme heat, molten spatter, cut risks, and pinch points using aluminized and composite gloves, cotton lubrication swabs, PAPRs, and heat-reflective gear.
Annealing & Cold End Inspection – Mitigates stress cracks, glass dust, and noise through cut-resistant PPE, particulate respirators, hearing protection, and precision swabs/brushes.
Maintenance & Repair – Protects against electrical hazards, confined spaces, chemicals, and falls with dielectric/arc-flash PPE, harnesses, chemical gloves, respirators, and non-shedding swabs.
Packaging, Logistics & Recycling – Addresses ergonomic lifting, crush and cut hazards, dust, and chemical residues via ergonomic impact gloves, chainmail and cut-resistant gear, safety boots, dust respirators, and quick-change swabs.
By offering gloves, respirators, swabs, and ancillary PPE tailored to each operational risk, Hand Line ensures regulatory compliance, minimizes downtime, and fosters a culture of safety across all production stages.

1. Raw Material Handling & Batching
Operators receive, store, and accurately weigh raw ingredients—silica sand, soda ash, limestone, and recycled cullet—often in bulk bags or silos.
Key Hazards:
Dust Inhalation: Fine silica and other mineral dusts become airborne during transfer and weighing, posing respiratory and long-term silicosis risks.
Ergonomic Strain: Repetitive lifting of heavy sacks or manipulating bulk container fittings can lead to musculoskeletal injuries.
Chemical Exposure: Additives (e.g., sodium sulfate, cullet residues) may irritate skin or eyes upon contact.
PPE Solutions:
P3/HEPA Respirators or PAPR Units to filter respirable silica and dusts, mitigating inhalation hazards.
Chemical-Resistant Gloves (Nitrile/Neoprene) for handling additives that could cause skin irritation.
Ergonomic Gloves with Padded Palms to cushion and improve grip, reducing hand fatigue during repetitive movements.
High-Efficiency Dust Swabs for sampling and cleaning fine dust accumulations without re-aerosolizing particles.

2. Hot End & Forming Operations (Cave-Glass Bottles)
Molten glass is melted in furnaces >1,500 °C, conditioned, and delivered to molds. Workers adjust refractories, stir melts, lubricate molds with cotton swabs; then molten glass is formed into bottles and transferred—manually or robotically—to annealing lehrs.
Key Hazards:
Thermal Burns & Radiant Heat: Contact with furnaces, molds, or spatter causes severe burns.
Molten Spatter: Droplets of molten glass can eject during stirring or mold filling.
Contact Heat During Lubrication: Applying release agents with cotton swabs to hot molds exposes hands to contact and radiant heat.
Cut & Abrasion Injuries: Sharp edges on freshly formed bottles or breakages.
Crush/Pinch Points: During robotic pick-and-place or manual handling of hot bottles.
Fume Exposure: Emissions of silica, metal oxides, and combustion byproducts pose inhalation risks.
PPE Solutions:
High-Heat, High-Contact Resistant Gloves: Aluminized, Kevlar-reinforced gauntlets with insulated liners and reinforced back-of-hand protection for mold lubrication and bottle transfers.
Cut- & Heat-Resistant Composite Gloves: Combine HPPE fibers and heat-insulating liners to protect against lacerations and surface heat during handling.
Cotton Swabs for Mold Lubrication: High-temp cotton swabs designed to carry release agents, resisting degradation and minimizing hand exposure.
PAPRs with High-Temperature Silicone Seals: Safe breathing in hot, particulate-laden atmospheres.
Heat-Reflective Clothing & Full-Face Shields: Deflect radiant heat and guard against spatter.
Mechanical-Assist Transfer Gloves: Improve grip control on hot, slippery surfaces, reducing pinch risks.
N95/N100 Respirators: Filter fine glass particulates from mold release agents or dust.
Lint-Free Inspection Swabs: For quality checks, ensuring no fibers contaminate the bottle surface.

3. Annealing & Cold End Inspection
Bottles cool gradually in lehrs; afterwards, visual and automated inspections detect defects.
Key Hazards:
Thermal Stress Cracks: Sharp fragments can form as glass cools unevenly.
Glass Dust Exposure: Automated grinding or defect removal generates respirable particles.
High Noise Levels: Conveyor and inspection machinery contribute to elevated dB levels.
PPE Solutions:
Cut-Resistant Sleeves & Gloves to protect against sharp stress cracks during manual inspection.
Dust & Particulate Respirators to filter airborne glass dust from grinding and defect removal.
Hearing Protection (Earplugs/Earmuffs) to attenuate noise above safe thresholds.
Inspection Swabs & Brushes for precise removal of chips without spreading debris.

4. Maintenance & Repair Maintenance & Repair. Maintenance & Repair
Planned or emergency work on furnaces, lehrs, conveyors, and electrical systems.
Key Hazards:
Confined Space Entry: Oxygen deficiency or toxic atmospheres in furnace cavities.
Electrical Shock & Arc Flash: Live-line work on high-voltage components.
Chemical Contact: Cleaning solvents and refractory binders.
Height & Fall Risks: Servicing elevated sections of equipment.
PPE Solutions:
Dielectric Electrical Gloves (Class 2/3) for energized work up to specified kV.
Arc-Flash Rated Suits & Face Shields to guard against flash burns and projectiles.
Full-Body Harnesses & Lanyards for fall arrest during elevated maintenance.
Chemical-Resistant Gloves & Respirators for solvent handling and fume protection.
Non-Shedding Industrial Swabs for cleaning electrical contacts to maintain conductivity.

5. Packaging, Logistics & Recycling
After inspection, bottles are packed into cartons or crates, palletized, and either shipped or sent for recycling processing. Waste streams (cullet, rejects, slag) are collected, screened, and prepared for reuse.
Key Hazards:
Ergonomic Strain: Manual lifting of cases, pallets, and waste containers can cause musculoskeletal injuries.
Crush & Drop Hazards: Bottles, cases, pallets, or heavy cullet may fall, risking foot and limb injuries.
Sharp Shards & Abrasions: Broken bottles and slag fragments pose cut risks.
Dust & Silica Exposure: Handling cullet and rejects generates fine particulates.
Chemical Residues: Waste glass may carry residues from prior processing.
PPE Solutions:
Ergonomic Impact-Reducing Gloves: Padded gloves to reduce vibration and fatigue during lifting and packing.
Cut-Resistant Sleeves & Chainmail Gloves: Combined solutions for forearms and hands to guard against shards.
Metatarsal & Steel-Toe Safety Boots: Protect feet from dropped objects and chemical exposure.
P3/HEPA Dust Respirators & Safety Glasses: Filter fine dust while shielding eyes from debris.
Quick-Change Dust & Contamination Swabs: For swift residue sampling and cleanup without re-aerosolizing particles.

La fabrication du verre exige une protection exceptionnelle des mains, particulièrement dans les opérations Hot End où les températures dépassent 1000°C. Notre gamme spécialisée couvre toute la chaîne de production, de la manipulation du verre en fusion au traitement du produit fini, avec plus de 25 solutions spécialisées développées à travers des décennies d'expertise dans l'industrie.

## Notre technologie de protection spécialisée

Les gants HandLine pour l'industrie du verre intègrent notre technologie GlassGuard™, caractérisée par:

- Protection thermique avancée maintenant la dextérité jusqu'à 1000°C dans les opérations Hot End
- Motif de préhension en silicone spécialisé pour manipulation sûre des produits en verre
- Construction de doublure sans couture pour prévenir la contamination par fibres de verre
- Design de gantelet prolongé avec protection renforcée du poignet

english: Steel production presents some of the most demanding safety challenges in industrial manufacturing. Workers are routinely exposed to extreme heat, molten metal splashes, high noise levels, sharp and heavy materials, and airborne contaminants such as metal fumes and dust. Each stage of the process — from furnace operations to rolling and finishing — introduces unique risks that can cause severe burns, cuts, respiratory issues, and impact injuries if not properly controlled. Effective protection therefore relies on specialized PPE designed for high heat, cut resistance, chemical handling, and respiratory safety, combined with strict adherence to safety procedures and continuous worker training to ensure long-term protection in these harsh environments.
italian: La produzione dell’acciaio presenta alcune delle sfide di sicurezza più impegnative nell’ambito industriale. Gli operatori sono regolarmente esposti a calore estremo, schizzi di metallo fuso, livelli elevati di rumore, materiali taglienti e pesanti, oltre a contaminanti aerodispersi come fumi e polveri metalliche. Ogni fase del processo — dalla fusione alla laminazione e finitura — comporta rischi specifici che possono causare ustioni gravi, tagli, problemi respiratori e traumi da impatto se non adeguatamente controllati. Una protezione efficace richiede quindi DPI specializzati per la resistenza al calore, al taglio, alle sostanze chimiche e per la sicurezza respiratoria, insieme a rigorose procedure di sicurezza e a una formazione continua dei lavoratori per garantire una protezione duratura in ambienti tanto difficili.
